title: Anatomy-preserving unpaired cone-beam CT refinement for image-guided radiotherapy using pseudo-label guided diffusion
title_zh: 基于伪标签引导扩散的解剖结构保留型非配对锥形束CT图像优化：用于图像引导放射治疗的研究

paragraphs.en: Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is widely used in image-guided radiotherapy, yet its broader clinical utility is limited by scatter, beam hardening, noise, truncation, and other artifacts that degrade image quality and CT-number fidelity. Although deep learning methods have shown promise for CBCT correction, most rely on paired CBCT–CT training data, which are difficult to obtain in routine clinical practice because of motion, anatomical variation, and acquisition mismatch. Here we present RefineCBCT, an unpaired CBCT refinement framework that combines pseudo-label guidance with short-step diffusion to suppress artifacts while preserving patient-specific anatomy. By formulating CBCT correction as anatomy-preserving refinement rather than unconstrained image translation, RefineCBCT provides structurally consistent guidance for diffusion-based restoration under unpaired supervision.
paragraphs.zh: 锥形束计算机断层扫描（CBCT）广泛应用于图像引导放射治疗，但其更广泛的临床效用受到散射、束硬化、噪声、截断及其他会降低图像质量和CT值准确性的伪影的限制。 尽管深度学习方法在CBCT校正方面展现出潜力，但大多数方法依赖于配对的CBCT–CT训练数据，而这些数据因运动、解剖学差异和采集不匹配等问题，在日常临床实践中难以获取。 本文提出RefineCBCT，一种无配对的CBCT优化框架，该框架将伪标签引导与短步长扩散相结合，在抑制伪影的同时保留患者特定的解剖结构。 通过将CBCT校正定义为保留解剖结构的优化而非无约束的图像转换，RefineCBCT在无配对监督下为基于扩散的恢复提供了结构一致的指导。

paragraphs.en: RefineCBCT was trained and evaluated using unpaired CBCT and planning CT data from the public LUNG TCIA and PELVIC TCIA datasets and compared with representative GAN-based and diffusion-based methods. On LUNG TCIA, RefineCBCT achieved the best performance across all evaluated metrics, with a mean absolute error of 19.411, root mean squared error of 62.758, peak signal-to-noise ratio of 30.845 dB, and structural similarity index of 0.931. On PELVIC TCIA, it achieved the best mean absolute error, peak signal-to-noise ratio, and structural similarity index, with values of 14.905, 36.671 dB, and 0.876, respectively. The refined images showed reduced streaking and shading artifacts, clearer anatomical boundaries, and improved soft-tissue uniformity. Line-profile and region-of-interest analyses further demonstrated closer agreement with planning CT in both bone and soft-tissue regions.

paragraphs.en: Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is routinely used in image-guided radiotherapy because it provides fast, on-board volumetric imaging during treatment Zhao et al. (2026) ; Kapila et al. (2011) ; Purdie et al. (2007) ; Hvid et al. (2018) ; Allen et al. (2023) . However, despite its convenience and widespread availability, CBCT is still used mainly for patient setup and coarse localization rather than for quantitative or decision-critical applications Zhang et al. (2023) ; Zhong et al. (2023) ; Wu et al. (2022) ; Weiss and Read-Fuller (2019) ; Quereshy et al. (2008) ; De Vos et al. (2009) ; Hirota et al. (2006) . The main reason is that CBCT suffers from severe image degradation, including scatter, beam hardening, noise, truncation, and motion-related corruption, which lead to streaking artifacts, shading, blurred boundaries, low soft-tissue contrast, and inaccurate intensities Hsieh et al. (2000) ; Jarry et al. (2006) ; Zhang et al. (2007) ; Sisniega et al. (2017) ; Song et al. (2025) . These limitations reduce confidence in downstream tasks such as contouring, dose evaluation, adaptive planning, and automated analysis. Therefore, the key clinical question is not whether CBCT can be acquired, but whether routinely acquired CBCT can be refined into an image that is reliable enough for broader clinical use Lin et al. (2023) ; Su et al. (2023) .

paragraphs.en: This makes unpaired CBCT refinement more clinically realistic, but also substantially more challenging. Without voxel-wise targets, the model must suppress artifacts while preserving patient-specific anatomy. In medical imaging, this requirement is crucial: a visually cleaner image is not useful if clinically relevant structures are hallucinated, displaced, or over-smoothed. Existing unpaired translation methods can improve appearance, but often lack sufficient control over anatomical consistency and restoration stability Zhu et al. (2017) ; Bashkirova et al. (2019) ; You et al. (2020) . Diffusion models offer strong generative priors and powerful restoration capability, but in unpaired CBCT enhancement they still need effective guidance to avoid drifting away from the input anatomy, and their iterative sampling cost can limit practical deployment Özbey et al. (2023) ; Li et al. (2023a) ; Chung et al. (2023) ; Zhao et al. (2024) ; Li et al. (2025) .
paragraphs.zh: 这使得无配对的CBCT优化在临床上更具现实性，但也带来了显著更大的挑战。在没有体素级目标的情况下，模型必须抑制伪影，同时保留患者特定的解剖结构。在医学成像中，这一要求至关重要：如果临床相关的结构被幻觉生成、移位或过度平滑，那么图像在视觉上更清晰也没有实际意义。现有的无配对转换方法虽然能够改善外观，但通常缺乏对解剖一致性和恢复稳定性的充分控制 Zhu et al. (2017) ; Bashkirova et al. (2019) ; You et al. (2020) 。扩散模型提供了强大的生成先验和卓越的恢复能力，但在无配对的CBCT增强中，它们仍然需要有效的引导以避免偏离输入的解剖结构，并且其迭代采样成本可能会限制实际部署 Özbey et al. (2023) ; Li et al. (2023a) ; Chung et al. (2023) ; Zhao et al. (2024) ; Li et al. (2025) 。

paragraphs.en: To address these issues, we propose RefineCBCT , an unpaired CBCT refinement framework guided by pseudo labels and short-step diffusion, as shown in Fig. 1 . The method is built on a simple idea: unpaired refinement should be constrained enough to preserve anatomy, but flexible enough to remove complex artifacts. To achieve this, RefineCBCT first uses a pseudo-label translation module to generate anatomy-preserving intermediate references from unpaired clinical CT data. These pseudo labels provide a stable supervisory bridge in the absence of paired CBCT-CT correspondence. RefineCBCT then applies a short-step diffusion refinement module to perform controlled denoising and artifact suppression, improving image fidelity while avoiding unconstrained image generation. This design makes the framework not only anatomically aware, but also more computationally efficient than long-horizon diffusion restoration, which is important for clinical usability.
paragraphs.zh: 为解决这些问题，我们提出了 RefineCBCT——一种由伪标签和短步扩散引导的非配对 CBCT 优化框架，如图 1 所示。 该方法基于一个简单的理念：非配对优化应受到足够约束以保留解剖结构，但又需足够灵活以去除复杂的伪影。 为实现这一目标，RefineCBCT 首先使用一个伪标签转换模块，从非配对的临床 CT 数据中生成能够保留解剖结构的中间参考图像。 在没有配对 CBCT-CT 对应关系的情况下，这些伪标签提供了一个稳定的监督桥梁。 随后，RefineCBCT 应用短步扩散优化模块进行受控的去噪和伪影抑制，在提升图像保真度的同时避免无约束的图像生成。 这种设计使该框架不仅具备解剖结构感知能力，而且比长时程扩散恢复方法在计算效率上更高，这对临床实用性至关重要。

paragraphs.en: The methodological highlight of RefineCBCT lies in the explicit coupling of designing around three priorities that are often difficult to satisfy simultaneously in unpaired medical image enhancement: fidelity , robustness , and efficiency . The translated pseudo-label is not treated as a final synthetic image or as fixed offline supervision. Instead, it provides a structural constraint that is jointly updated with the diffusion model. The reconstruction objective preserves CBCT intensity information, the cycle-consistency objective maintains cross-domain anatomy, and the time-conditional adversarial objective regularizes short-step diffusion transitions. This joint design is intended to prevent errors in the pseudo-label from propagating directly to the corrected image, thereby balancing artifact suppression, anatomical fidelity, and computational efficiency. The main contributions are as follows:

sents.en: The reconstruction objective preserves CBCT intensity information, the cycle-consistency objective maintains cross-domain anatomy, and the time-conditional adversarial objective regularizes short-step diffusion transitions.

paragraphs.en: i) We propose RefineCBCT , a CBCT enhancement framework that formulates the task as an anatomically constrained refinement problem and learns from unpaired CT and CBCT data without requiring voxel-wise aligned supervision. Specifically, the method integrates a consistency-aware pseudo-label guidance strategy, which couples bidirectional CT–CBCT translation with conditional diffusion to guide artifact suppression while reducing structural distortion and hallucination, together with a short-step diffusion refinement process that lowers sampling cost while maintaining stable restoration. In this way, RefineCBCT achieves anatomically faithful and computationally efficient CBCT refinement, offering a practical balance between image quality, structural preservation, and clinical usability.
paragraphs.zh: i) 我们提出了 RefineCBCT，这是一种 CBCT 增强框架。该框架将任务表述为一个具有解剖学约束的优化问题，并通过未配对的 CT 和 CBCT 数据进行学习，无需体素级对齐的监督。 具体而言，该方法整合了一种一致性感知伪标签引导策略：它将双向 CT–CBCT 转换与条件扩散相结合，以引导抑制伪影，同时减少结构失真和幻觉；此外，还采用了一个短步长扩散优化过程，在保持稳定重建效果的同时降低了采样成本。 通过这种方式，RefineCBCT 实现了在解剖学上忠实且计算高效的 CBCT 优化，在图像质量、结构保留和临床可用性之间取得了实用的平衡。

paragraphs.en: The qualitative results further support these findings. In the lung cases shown in Fig. 7(a) , the detection task involves both a relatively large target region in the spine and small rounded nodular structures in the lung. In the original CBCT images, undersampling-induced streak artifacts severely degrade image quality, leading to poor identification of both target types. Most comparison methods improve the overall depiction of the spine, but their recovery of the small nodular structures remains limited. In contrast, RefineCBCT better preserves these subtle small-scale structures while maintaining the morphology of the larger target, which is consistent with its superior quantitative detection performance. This suggests that the proposed method is more effective in recovering fine anatomical details that are critical for small-target recognition.

paragraphs.en: Although CT and CBCT are inherently three-dimensional, RefineCBCT processes each axial slice independently using a 2D network. The corrected slices are subsequently reassembled into volumes to generate the sagittal and coronal views shown in Fig. 8 . These improvements are particularly evident on the LUNG TCIA dataset, where streaking and shading artifacts are more pronounced. Minor differences between sCBCT and pCT may remain because of registration errors and inter-scan anatomical variation.

paragraphs.en: The slice-wise design reduces memory consumption and computational complexity relative to fully 3D processing, which is important for high-resolution CBCT refinement. paragraphs.en: Nevertheless, the current framework does not explicitly model correlations between adjacent slices. Consequently, subtle through-plane inconsistencies may occur, particularly in regions with rapid anatomical changes, patient motion, or severe artifacts. paragraphs.en: Future work will extend RefineCBCT to 2.5D and 3D formulations. A 2.5D model could incorporate neighboring slices while retaining relatively low computational cost, whereas a fully 3D model could directly learn volumetric context and enforce through-plane structural continuity. Cross-slice consistency losses may provide another efficient alternative. These extensions will be evaluated using volumetric consistency measures and downstream tasks such as 3D segmentation, registration, contouring, and dose calculation.

paragraphs.en: To balance reconstruction fidelity and computational efficiency, we adopted a short diffusion schedule. Unless otherwise specified, the number of sampling steps was set to K = 4 K=4 , which provided a favorable trade-off between image quality and inference time in our experiments. paragraphs.en: In this study, we proposed RefineCBCT, an unpaired CBCT refinement framework that combines pseudo-label guidance with short-step diffusion to improve image quality while preserving anatomical structures. Across two public datasets, RefineCBCT achieved better overall performance than several GAN-based and diffusion-based baseline methods. The method reduced common CBCT artifacts, improved visual image quality, and produced images with CT values that were closer to planning CT. These results suggest that RefineCBCT is a promising approach for CBCT enhancement in realistic unpaired training settings.

paragraphs.en: An important feature of this work is that CBCT enhancement is treated as a refinement task rather than an unrestricted image generation. In medical imaging, good visual appearance alone is not enough ; the enhanced image must also preserve patient-specific anatomy. In RefineCBCT, the pseudo-label translation module provides structural guidance for the diffusion process, and cycle-consistency helps reduce anatomical distortion during unpaired learning. The improvements in SSIM, visual quality, and HU consistency suggest that this design helps balance artifact reduction with anatomical fidelity.

paragraphs.en: This study has several limitations . i) the experiments were performed on two public datasets with a limited number of patients, and the model was trained in a 2D slice-by-slice manner rather than in full 3D; ii) planning CT was used as the reference, but mismatch between CBCT and pCT may still affect evaluation; iii) although image quality and HU consistency improved, we did not test downstream clinical tasks such as segmentation, dose calculation, or adaptive radiotherapy planning. Therefore, the present results should be interpreted as showing technical feasibility rather than direct clinical benefit. In addition, the robustness of the method across scanners, institutions, and imaging protocols still needs further validation.

paragraphs.en: In conclusion, RefineCBCT provides an effective and efficient method for unpaired CBCT refinement. By combining pseudo-label guidance with short-step diffusion, it improves image quality, reduces artifacts, and better preserves anatomical structure without requiring paired CBCT-CT training data. These findings support the potential of clinically oriented diffusion-based refinement for CBCT enhancement and motivate future validation in larger and more diverse clinical settings.

paragraphs.en: We propose RefineCBCT , introduced a pseudo-label diffusion model for unpaired cone-beam CT (CBCT) refinement task. The method is designed to improve CBCT image quality while preserving anatomical structures, with particular emphasis on robustness , computational efficiency , and practical potential for clinical use. paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 RefineCBCT，这是一种用于无配对的锥形束 CT（CBCT）优化任务的伪标签扩散模型。 该方法旨在提升 CBCT 图像质量的同时保留解剖结构，并特别注重鲁棒性、计算效率以及临床应用的实践潜力。 如图 10 所示，RefineCBCT 整合了两个紧密耦合的组件：i) 一个循环一致的伪标签转换模块，用于连接 CT 和 CBCT 域并提供基于解剖结构的指导；ii) 一个短步长条件扩散优化模块，可逐步抑制伪影并恢复类 CT 图像质量。

paragraphs.en: The pseudo-label translation module contains two image-to-image generators, CT → \rightarrow CBCT and CBCT → \rightarrow CT, each paired with a local PatchGAN-style discriminator. This branch produces pseudo-labels that provide domain-consistent structural guidance without requiring paired CBCT/CT supervision. The diffusion refinement module consists of a conditional generator operating with a small number of diffusion steps and a time-conditional discriminator that evaluates adjacent noisy states at a given timestep. To maintain a simple and efficient pipeline, all inputs are processed as single 2D slices, padded to a uniform spatial size and normalized to [ − 1 , 1 ] [-1,1] .

paragraphs.en: A key challenge in unpaired CBCT refinement is the lack of voxel-wise aligned CBCT/CT supervision. To address this, RefineCBCT incorporates a pseudo-label translation module that learns bidirectional mapping between the CBCT domain 𝒳 \mathcal{X} and the CT domain 𝒞 \mathcal{C} . paragraphs.en: During training, the translation generators ( G α , G α ′ ) (G_{\alpha},G^{\prime}_{\alpha}) , diffusion generator G β G_{\beta} , and discriminators ( D α , D α ′ , D β ) (D_{\alpha},D^{\prime}_{\alpha},D_{\beta}) are optimized in an alternating manner.
